name: Organizing Storage
description: Properly sorts incoming wholesale flower crates and botanical stems into species-specific microenvironments to extend vase life and prevent chilling or chemical damage. Key parameters include routing temperate blooms and foliage to refrigerated cold storage at 2°C–4°C, tropical stems to an ambient bench at 13°C–18°C, and Narcissus varieties to an isolated water vessel.

learned_parameters.label: Dutch White Lilies (Lilium orientalis)
learned_parameters.rationale: Must be stored in the Floral Cooler (2°C–4°C). In Attempt #1 and #2, setting the cooler yielded a 100/100 item score. In Attempt #3, placing lilies on the Ambient Tropical Bench dropped the item score to 0/100, with feedback indicating petal firmness and bud life rapidly degrade outside high-humidity refrigeration. Measured: Tried: 'Floral Cooler (2°C–4°C)' (100/100), 'Ambient Tropical Bench' (0/100).

learned_parameters.label: Anthurium Blooms
learned_parameters.rationale: Must be stored on the Ambient Tropical Bench (13°C–18°C). In Attempt #1, placement in the Floral Cooler scored 0/100 due to black chilling spots and petal necrosis below 10°C. In Attempt #4, placing them in the Narcissus Isolation Vessel scored 0/100. In Attempt #2, assigning to the Ambient Tropical Bench scored 100/100. Measured: Tried: 'Floral Cooler (2°C–4°C)' (0/100), 'Ambient Tropical Bench' (100/100), 'Narcissus Isolation Vessel' (0/100).

learned_parameters.label: Paperwhite Jonquils (Narcissus tazetta)
learned_parameters.rationale: Must be placed in the Narcissus Isolation Vessel. In Attempt #2, this assignment scored 100/100. In Attempt #5, placing paperwhites into the Floral Cooler scored 0/100 because their sap contains lycorine alkaloids that contaminate standard water. Measured: Tried: 'Narcissus Isolation Vessel' (100/100), 'Floral Cooler (2°C–4°C)' (0/100).

learned_parameters.label: Vanda Orchids
learned_parameters.rationale: Must be placed on the Ambient Tropical Bench (13°C–18°C). In Attempt #1, placing them in the Floral Cooler scored 0/100 due to rapid floret loss and chilling injury. In Attempt #6, placing them in the Narcissus Isolation Vessel scored 0/100. Assigning them to the Ambient Tropical Bench achieved 100/100 in Attempt #2. Measured: Tried: 'Floral Cooler (2°C–4°C)' (0/100), 'Ambient Tropical Bench' (100/100), 'Narcissus Isolation Vessel' (0/100).

learned_parameters.label: Freedom Red Roses (Rosa)
learned_parameters.rationale: Must be placed in the Floral Cooler (2°C–4°C). In Attempt #2, this assignment scored 100/100. In Attempt #7, moving roses to the Ambient Tropical Bench dropped the sub-score to 0/100 because ambient warmth accelerates respiration and causes premature bloom opening. Measured: Tried: 'Floral Cooler (2°C–4°C)' (100/100), 'Ambient Tropical Bench' (0/100).

learned_parameters.label: Eucalyptus Foliage Bunches
learned_parameters.rationale: Must be placed in the Floral Cooler (2°C–4°C). In Attempt #2, this yielded 100/100. In Attempt #8, moving eucalyptus to the Ambient Tropical Bench reduced the sub-score to 0/100 because temperate greens wilt and dry out prematurely without chilled storage. Measured: Tried: 'Floral Cooler (2°C–4°C)' (100/100), 'Ambient Tropical Bench' (0/100).

steps: Unpack arriving floral crates and inspect incoming species labels before bucket preparation.

Route temperate cut stems and foliage—including Dutch White Lilies (Lilium orientalis), Freedom Red Roses (Rosa), and Eucalyptus Foliage Bunches—directly into the Floral Cooler maintained between 2°C and 4°C.
Route chilling-sensitive tropical flowers—specifically Anthurium Blooms and Vanda Orchids—onto the Ambient Tropical Bench maintained between 13°C and 18°C.

Isolate all sap-bleeding Narcissus family varieties—specifically Paperwhite Jonquils (Narcissus tazetta) and Fresh-cut Golden Daffodils (Narcissus)—into dedicated Narcissus Isolation Vessels for at least 12 hours before considering any integration with other stems.
caveats: Never place tropical blooms (Anthuriums or Vanda Orchids) below 10°C; floral cooler refrigeration causes rapid floret drop and irreversible black necrosis.

Never co-condition Narcissus species with other flowers in standard cooler buckets; freshly cut daffodil and paperwhite stems secrete mucilage containing toxic lycorine alkaloids that clog vascular tissues of companion stems.
Do not leave temperate garden flowers or foliage at room temperature; warm ambient exposure accelerates respiration and blossom opening while desiccating foliage.
Tropical flowers (Anthuriums, Vanda orchids) require warmer ambient bench conditions (13°C–18°C) rather than cold floral coolers.
Narcissus species (daffodils, jonquils) release sap toxic to other flowers and must always go into the isolation vessel.
Tropical flowers (Anthuriums, Vanda orchids) must stay on the ambient tropical bench to avoid chilling injury.
Narcissus varieties must always be placed into the narcissus isolation vessel to protect other stems from toxic mucilage.

Standard cut flowers and foliage (Roses, Lilies, Eucalyptus) thrive best in the cold floral cooler (2°C–4°C).

problems.problem: Anthuriums suffer irreversible black chilling spots and petal necrosis if placed below 10°C.
problems.fix: Remove Anthurium blooms from refrigerated coolers immediately and store them on the Ambient Tropical Bench between 13°C and 18°C.

problems.problem: Tropical orchids drop florets and experience rapid chilling damage inside a standard floral cooler.
Anthurium Blooms suffer chilling injury below 10°C and must not be stored in the standard floral cooler.
Vanda Orchids drop florets in floral cooler temperatures and need warm ambient storage.
Lilies preserve petal firmness and bud life best in standard high-humidity refrigerated storage.
Placing Lilies outside the floral cooler causes loss of petal firmness and bud life.
Anthuriums cannot be placed in the isolation vessel or cold storage; they require the warm ambient tropical bench.
Paperwhites release sap containing lycorine alkaloid; they must condition in isolated water for 12 hours before sharing vases.
Paperwhites placed in the floral cooler contaminate standard water and drop score to 0.
(attempt 6) Placing Vanda Orchids in the Narcissus Isolation Vessel fails to satisfy their storage and temperature requirements.
Temperate garden flowers like roses must be held near freezing to slow respiration and halt rapid blossom opening.
Hardy greens and temperate cut foliage stay crisp and dormant inside the refrigerated cooler.
Hardy greens and temperate foliage wilt and lose crispness when placed outside the floral cooler at ambient temperatures.
